lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants. 
Ex parte—Respondent
parties:
Matiar Rahman ----- Appellants
Vs.
Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property Lands and Buildings ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 8. In the petition for review it was stated that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 634 of 1970 is claiming the property on the basis of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 198 of 1970, which was filed averring that the land in suit orally was settled to him by the recorded tenants, that the suit i.e. Title Suit No. 634 of 1970, was contested by the defendant No. 2, i.e. petitioner in the review petition, whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1980 was registered, primarily contending that the recorded tenants of the property left for West Bengal, India and thereupon the property in question was treated as enemy property and that some of the recorded tenants died long before obtaining decree in Title Suit No. 198 of 1970, that the solenama on the basis of which Title Suit No. 198 of 1970 was decreed was a fraudulent one and that the said solenama was said to have been signed by persons who died long before filing of the Title Suit No. 198 of 1970, that the government is in possession of the property on the basis of Requisition Case No. 55 of 1959, that during the trial as well as at the time of hearing of the appeal in spite of exercising due diligence could not bring on record the vital papers, i.e. the record of the Requisition Case No. 55 of 1959 and the death certificate of Sreenath Chatterjee, who died on July 24, 1947.
